reasoning: Matrix sample columns are MPST1, MPST2, MPST3, MPST4, MST1, MST3, MST4, R11, R20, R23, R26, R29, R2, R4. Metadata identifies samples only by GSM id, title ('Physical exercise group_rep1', 'Culture medium injection group rep1', ...), and source_name ('Ischemic striatum from PE+Vehicle-1', 'NPCs+PE-1', ...). No metadata field (index, title, source_name, description, relation) contains these lab codes, and the SRA records (SRX13339692-705, runinfo efetch) carry no LibraryName. So no exact key exists. A decoding guess is possible for 7 columns (MPST = MCAO+PE+Stem-cell Transplant, 4 columns = NPCs+PE n=4; MST = MCAO+Stem-cell Transplant, 3 columns = NPCs alone n=3) but the replicate numbers do not even match (MST1/3/4 vs NPCs-1/2/3), and the 7 R columns (R2, R4, R11, R20, R23, R26, R29) carry no information on which 4 are vehicle+PE and which 3 are vehicle alone. The paper's primary exercise contrast (Fig 5A, vehicle+PE vs vehicle) is therefore unidentifiable from the deposited data, and the Fig 5D contrast would rest on an abbreviation guess, not an exact key. Position-based or guessed alignment is not allowed. Stopped for manual review: the authors' column-to-group key (or the per-sample raw counts from SRA re-quantification) would unblock it.
stop_reason: No exact key between matrix columns (MPST*/MST*/R*) and GEO samples; the 7 R* columns cannot be assigned to vehicle+PE vs vehicle, so the paper's exercise contrast (Fig 5A) is unidentifiable. Needs the authors' sample-code key or SRA re-quantification.
